content: The Board may either revise or accept the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), the task order, and/or portions of the ABRWH's independent dose reconstruction review of contractor bids. These contracts are intended to provide technical support and consultation to assist the Advisory Board on Radiation and Worker Health (ABRWH) in fulfilling its statutory obligation to advise the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on the scientific validity and quality of dose estimation and reconstruction efforts under the Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act (EEOICPA). The discussions will involve reviews of technical proposals to assess the adequacy of the proposed approaches and the associated cost estimates for the contracts. The information under discussion will include confidential material. Consequently, the meeting will be closed to the public in accordance with the confidentiality provisions outlined in 5 U.S.C. 552b(c)(9)(B), 48 CFR 5.401(b)(1) and (4), and 48 CFR 7.304(D), as well as the Determination of the Director of the Management Analysis and Services Office, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pursuant to Public Law 92-463. A summary of the meeting will be prepared and submitted within 14 days of its conclusion. The agenda may be subject to change based on shifting priorities. 1. Ceiling-5M and Analytical Cycle Times: A reviewer expressed concern that the 5-minute ceiling (Ceiling-5M) might require an analytical cycle too short for dual-agent air monitoring instruments. The Ceiling-5M was designed to provide a near-real-time corrective action threshold to protect worker health in the short term while maintaining a long-term carcinogenicity risk below one in a million. The CDC evaluated the impact of longer cycle times (10–15 minutes) on the concentration-time (Ct) product and found that both short-term and long-term health protection goals were still met.003 mg/m³, monitored using NRT technology with the shortest feasible cycle time. The Ct for the 15-minute STEL is 0.045 mg-min/m³. 2. General Population Limit (GPL) for Worker Protection: A reviewer noted that using the proposed GPL for worker protection could lead to excessive false positives and operational disruptions. The GPL is designed to protect the general public, accounting for greater variability in susceptibility compared to the healthy worker population. The CDC proposed using the GPL for worker protection based on its adequacy for both populations and its historical use in demilitarization perimeter monitoring. The CDC now recommends a separate 8-hour TWA Worker Protection Limit (WPL) of 0.0004 mg/m³, derived from the U.S. Army Center for Health Promotion and Preventive Medicine (CHPPM) reference concentration, rather than applying the GPL. 3. Application of AELs Beyond Stockpile Demilitarization: The Army highlighted that the proposed AELs, while developed for stockpile demilitarization, might also apply to other non-stockpile and storage scenarios. 4. 5. Uncertainty Factors in AEL Derivation: Reviewers provided differing opinions on the use of uncertainty factors in deriving AELs, with some suggesting reductions and others advocating for increases. The CDC emphasized the importance of professional judgment in applying uncertainty factors and noted that its approach considered both risk assessment and risk management aspects. The agency acknowledged the need to balance theoretical safety with practical risk management to avoid increasing real-world risks. Summary and Recommendations: The CDC received four sets of comments on the proposed mustard AELs, focusing on both the development process and practical implications. The CDC concluded that the numeric estimation of a cancer slope factor for sulfur mustard is not well-supported and recommended interim AELs pending better data. Key recommendations include: Redesignating the Ceiling-5M as a 15-minute STEL with a concentration of 0.003 mg/m³. Adopting the CHPPM-derived 8-hour WPL for worker protection and retaining the GPL for public protection. Implementing the interim AELs effective July 1, 2005, with ongoing evaluation and potential revision based on new data. Deferring the recommendation of a definitive CPF until more accurate data becomes available. FDA Animal Drug User Fee Cover Sheet (Form 3547): Under the Animal Drug User Fee Act (ADUFA), the FDA requires the submission of user fees with animal drug applications and supplements. Applications without the required fees are considered incomplete and will not be reviewed. FDA Form 3547 collects essential information to determine fee requirements, link payments to applications, and initiate administrative screening. The form generates a unique payment identification number for tracking purposes. The FDA invites comments on the necessity, accuracy, and burden of this information collection process, as well as suggestions for improving its utility and minimizing respondent burden.
